claim.quote: Data obtained at Brookhaven National Laboratory, using nearly equal samples of positive and negative muons, were used to deduce a_mu(Expt) = 11 659 208.0(5.4)(3.3) x 10^-10, where the statistical and systematic uncertainties are given, respectively.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal version is Phys. Rev. D 73, 072003 (2006).

name: Final Report of the Muon E821 Anomalous Magnetic Moment Measurement at BNL

significance.quote: Present standard model evaluations, based on e+e- hadronic cross sections, lie 2.2 - 2.7 standard deviations below the experimental result.
significance.value: Standard model evaluations based on e+e- hadronic cross sections lie 2.2 - 2.7 standard deviations below the experimental result

summary.plain: The Brookhaven experiment E821 measured how fast the muon’s spin turns in a magnetic field and gave the muon’s magnetic anomaly to a precision of 0.54 parts per million, fourteen times better than earlier CERN measurements. Standard Model calculations based on electron-positron data lay 2.2 to 2.7 standard deviations below it.
summary.technical: Final E821 report: a_mu(Expt) = 11 659 208.0(5.4)(3.3) x 10^-10 (0.54 ppm) from nearly equal samples of mu+ and mu-, a 14-fold improvement over CERN; standard model evaluations based on e+e- hadronic cross sections lie 2.2-2.7 standard deviations below the experimental result.

title: Final Report of the Muon E821 Anomalous Magnetic Moment Measurement at BNL
why_it_matters: The abstract says the largest theoretical uncertainty (about 0.55 ppm) is the first-order hadronic vacuum polarization, so the comparison tests the Standard Model at the level of virtual QED, weak and hadronic loops.
